'''Khanom salim''' (Thai: ขนมซาหริ่ม) is a traditional Thai [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]]. It consists of sweet colored [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|mung bean]] noodles served with coconut milk and crushed ice. Khanom Salim is one of the most famous Thai desserts due to its unique flavor, ingredients, and scent of jasmine.
== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Mung Bean|mung bean]] flour/starch<ref>{{cite web|title=Mungbean flour|url=http://www.wisegeek.org/what-is-mung-bean-flour.htm|website=wisegeek|publisher=wisegeek|accessdate=9 September 2014}}</ref>
* 5 cups (550 g) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|Food coloring]]

=== Simple syrup ===
* 2 cups (400 g) white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 1 cup (110 g) water
* 1 cup (150 g) [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]]
* [[Cookbook:Jasmine|Jasmine]] flavoring
* Crushed ice
== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Stovetop|Stove]]
* Salim press (used for making dough into noodles)<ref>{{cite web |title=Salim Press |url=http://www.templeofthai.com/cookware/salim-noodle-coconut-milk-6210000451.php |website=templeofthai}}</ref>
* Bowl (400 ml)
* Pan

== Procedure ==
# Mix the mung bean flour and water until smooth. Separate it into 2 or 3 portions, and mix 1–2 drops of food coloring into each portion to color it.
# Transfer each piece of dough into a pan, and put it on the stove over low heat.
# Stir constantly for about 15 minutes,until the dough is cooked and has become clear.
# Put all the dough in the salim press. Press the dough into a bowl of cold water.
# Make a simple [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]] by mixing the sugar and water together over a stove over low heat until the sugar is dissolved.
# Put the noodles into a small bowl with crushed ice. Top with jasmine-flavored coconut milk and the sugar syrup.
